finding: §7.1 makes the first task's acceptance "run scripts/check-measured-claims.py to exit 0 with no PENDING line ... matches the derivation as a set", but neither §7.1 nor the artifact pins WHERE in spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md the list lives, and the observer measures the union of every `file:function` line in the whole file rather than a designated list region. Verified by construction in a clone with the list written and the placeholder deleted: (a) a document whose visible "## The list (sweep scope)" section holds 20 entries with the other 80 buried in an HTML comment exits 0 with no PENDING; (b) a document with "## Superseded draft" (80 entries) followed by "## Final list" (20 entries) also exits 0 with no PENDING. Both are artifacts whose reader-visible scope is 20 while the check certifies 100. This matters beyond a contrived case because §7.1 itself hands the task triage ordering, so a conscientious first task will plausibly write scope sections (tier 1 / deferred, or in-scope / excluded-with-reason) — and an "excluded, not a guard" section still counts toward the set, so the check reports agreement over a document that declares a narrower cap than it certifies. §7.1's next sentence, "The sweep is capped at that list", then has no determinate referent for any later sweep task: two engineers reading the same passing artifact derive different sweep scopes.

resolved.evidence: The guard document now has a Guard tests heading and the check reads entries from that section only, so a draft or commented-out list elsewhere in the file is not part of the guard set. Mutation-tested: 20 entries under the heading with 80 in a comment above now fails.

suggestion: State in §7.1 that the file carries exactly one list, and name the region the acceptance is measured over — e.g. "every `file:function` line in the file is in scope; the file may not carry a second list, an excluded set, or commented-out entries" — so the guard's set and the sweep's cap are the same object by construction. If exclusions are wanted, say they are recorded in the closing evidence rather than in the file the check reads.

finding: §7.1 states the acceptance is "reachable only once the list is written, matches the derivation as a set, and the placeholder declaration is deleted" — three conditions the task controls. The observer has a fourth that the task does not control and that the spec never names: exit 0 also requires the repository-wide test-function count stated in §7.1 to still hold. Verified in a clone with the list correctly written: exit 0; then renaming a single test function anywhere in a tracked _test.go — the exact operation §7 mandates — turns it into exit 1 with "spec/0.34.0.md:177: states 1099, derivation gives 1098". So the first task's pass/fail depends on the execution order of unrelated tasks: §7.1 calls it "the release's first task" in prose only, and nothing in §7.1 or §12 requires every test-removing or test-adding task to depend on it. A tester cannot write a deterministic pass/fail for this acceptance — a red run means either the guard list is wrong or some other task closed first — and the only available repair for the second case is editing this spec's own number, which is precisely the "guard that teaches the wrong fix" shape §7.1's hazard paragraph is written to avoid. Not a claim that the number is currently stale; the defect is that the acceptance is coupled to a measurement this release exists to change.

resolved.evidence: The repository test-function count is removed from both the spec and the check. It was the fourth condition the guard-list task did not control, and this release removes tests, so the number would have been falsified by the work it describes with editing it as the only obvious repair. Mutation-tested: renaming a test elsewhere no longer affects the check.

suggestion: Either state the ordering constraint the acceptance depends on (every task that adds or removes a test function depends on the guard-list task, so the acceptance is evaluated before any §7 removal), or scope the acceptance to the object the task owns — e.g. "exit 0 with no PENDING line and no failure naming spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md" — so a repository count moved by a sibling task cannot fail the guard-list task.
